incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: increased 503s from dedicated-us-west pool starting at 23:41 UTC. Paging @maria (eng-oncall). Incident ID INC-20260317-01

maria (eng-oncall): On it. Jumping on bridge now: https://zoom.example/bridge-INC-20260317-01 - will post timeline here. @dan please grab routing logs.

dan (runtime): Joined bridge. Seeing a backlog in routing-compile queue, compile worker spike + OOM on 2 nodes. Restarting worker set 3.

ryan-sre: Restarting node-3 now. Will watch metrics.

allan (sre-manager): If restart fails, we should failover traffic to hosted-compatible model variants. Maria, suggest temporary routing policy update?

maria (eng-oncall): Agreed. Applying fallback policy to route new requests to model-variant v2-quant (higher cost) to keep latency. Apply 10% to fallback then ramp if needed.

dan (runtime): Applied 10% fallback via smart-routing. Monitoring KV cache hit changes and per-token latencies.

incident-bot: Status page draft ready for approval:
```
Service: Dedicated inference (us-west)
Impact: Elevated 503 errors and increased latency affecting dedicated customers
Mitigation: Temporary routing fallback to v2-quant; engineers restarting compile workers and clearing backlog
ETA: 30 minutes for validation and monitoring
```

amy (cs): Can we get a brief customer-safe blurb to post? Need wording for affected customers and whether we'll offer credits.

maria (eng-oncall): Customer blurb (short):
```
We're investigating elevated 503 errors affecting dedicated inference in US‑West. We've implemented a temporary routing fallback and are validating service stability. We'll provide follow-ups with timeline and corrective actions.
```

amy (cs): Thanks. Also drafting customer email for impacted accounts:
```
Subject: Brief outage notice — dedicated inference (US‑West)
Body: We observed elevated 503 errors between 23:41–00:12 UTC impacting dedicated inference. Mitigation steps included fallback routing and node restarts. We are continuing validation and will provide a post-incident RCA and preventative plan. Apologies for the disruption — customers can request SLA credit and our support team will assist.
```

krista (product): Do we want to include a specific SLA credit formula in the email? Ops: 10% monthly credit sounds reasonable for a partial degradation window.

allan (sre-manager): We should confirm exact windows and duration before promising credits.

dan (runtime): Node restarts succeeded, compile backlog cleared, 503s returned to baseline at 00:09 UTC. Continuing to monitor for regressions.

maria (eng-oncall): Confirmed stable at 00:12. Rolling fallback back down to 0% over 5 minutes.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in place, service restored. Status page state -> monitoring.

amy (cs): Draft RCA summary for customers:
```
RCA: Root cause was a compile-worker memory regression introduced by yesterday's runtime optimization which increased peak memory under routing-compile workloads. Two workers hit OOM which caused request queueing and resulting 503 responses.
Corrective actions: revert the memory-increasing change, add memory guardrails to compile workers, autoscale compile workers based on queue depth, add an alert for compile queue latency and OOMs.
Timeline: 23:41 detected -> 23:44 engineers paged -> 23:52 fallback routing applied -> 00:09 baseline restored -> 00:12 fallback rollback completed.
```
Please review and sign-off for customer notification.

maria (eng-oncall): Approve, except add a note about follow-up evals to prevent performance regressions under heavy compile traffic.

amy (cs): Added that line. Finalizing customer email and posting status page update. I'll send to impacted accounts and include support contact and steps to request SLA credit.

allan (sre-manager): :thumbsup: Good job everyone. Post-incident tasks: assign owner for guardrails (dan), run postmortem doc and timeline, confirm SLA impact calc and credit eligibility. I'll schedule the postmortem with stakeholders tomorrow morning.
